summary: Formalized a comprehensive architectural governance framework integrating the FIN rubric, DEBT.md manifest, and the Proactive Hotspot Identification System (PHIS). By shifting from reactive maintenance to proactive structural hardening—using AST-based analysis, git-churn metrics, and stability filters—Sam now quantifies architectural health through tangible output and high-ROI refactoring of high-complexity, high-churn modules.
key_learnings: AST-based parsing and structural hashing provide the most reliable defense against state-space ambiguity.
Representing knowledge as a DAG and enforcing quantitative constraints (FIN rubric) prevents cognitive overload.
Quantifying architectural health via DCS and churn-complexity correlation provides a predictive risk profile superior to static analysis alone.
Technical debt must be treated as a first-class entity with a quantifiable lifecycle to be effectively managed.
Refactoring ROI is maximized by targeting the intersection of high cognitive complexity and high version control churn while applying a 'Stability Filter' to avoid unnecessary changes to mature code.
Aligning progress metrics with specific architectural deliverables improves the clarity and accountability of autonomous development.
